Presence:-
Mr. Harshpal Sekhon, learned counsel for the petitioners
Mr. Anil Dabral, learned Additional C.S.C with Mr. Prem Prakash
Bhatt, learned Brief Holder for the State.
Hon'ble Pankaj Purohit, J.
These writ petitions have been filed by the
petitioner(s) seeking parity of pay scale with Data Entry
Operator working with the respondent employed through
U.P.N.L.
2. Since common questions of fact and law are
involved in these petitions, therefore, these petitions are
clubbed together and decided by this common judgment.
However, for the sake of brevity and convenience, facts of
WPSS No.1831 of 2026 alone are being considered and

UKHC010121712026
2026:UHC:6046
2
discussed.
3. Petitioner was engaged as a contractual Data
Entry Operator under the Samagra Shiksha Uttarakhand
at Block Resource Centre (B.R.C.) Mori, District
Uttarkashi. He was engaged on the said post on
03.05.2013 on contractual basis for a period of 11
months or till the end of Project under Sarva Shiksha
Abhiyan.
4. Petitioner was paid ₹5,500/- per month as
consolidate remuneration which was enhanced from time
to time and at present he is getting ₹18,000/- as
remuneration. The petitioner claimed parity with Data
Entry Operator who were engaged with the respondent
Department through U.P.N.L. and who are getting a
monthly remuneration of ₹27,299.63/-.
5. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits
that since the petitioner is discharging the same
functions as are being discharged by the Data Entry
Operator employed through U.P.N.L. therefore he is
entitled to get the same remuneration on the basis of
"equal pay for equal work".
6. Learned counsel for the petitioner further
submits that for the said relief the petitioner has filed a
representation to respondent no.2-State Project Director
for redressal of his grievance and he submits that if a
direction is issued to respondent no.2-State Project
Director to decide the said representation, within a
stipulated time, the ends of justice would be met.
7. Learned counsel for the State submits that the
representation which the petitioner has indicated has
been filed through his Union and therefore it would be
difficult for respondent no.2 to decide the same, however

UKHC010121712026
2026:UHC:6046
3
he submits that if the petitioner is permitted to file a
fresh representation to respondent no.2 within a
stipulated time, the respondent no.2 shall decide the
same if directed by the Court.
8. In such view of the matter, all the writ
petitions are finally disposed of. Petitioner(s) of each of
these writ petitions is permitted to file a representation
ventilating his grievance regarding equal pay for equal
work at par with the Data Entry Operator engaged
through U.P.N.L. within ten days' from today; and if such
a representation is submitted by the petitioner(s)
individually, the respondent no.2 shall decide the same
within a period of eight weeks' from the date of receipt of
the representations, strictly in accordance with law.
(Pankaj Purohit, J.
